label: 12:35 Cheltenham
race: Citipost Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 3) (Turf) 4YO+ 3m 1f Winner: £12,832 (10 runners)
note: Despite losing his unbeaten record over fences, LITTLE LEDGEND emerged with plenty of credit when third in a similar amateur riders' handicap over C&D 3 weeks ago. In a change of headgear he's marginally preferred to Herakles Westwood and Transmission, both of whom have previous in this race.

runners.tf_comment: Won 3m Southwell handicap chase in March 2025. Didn't fire in 3 runs last season and again folded alarmingly on last month's reappearance.

Thorough stayer who finally got off the mark in 10-runner handicap chase at Down Royal (3¼m, good to soft) in May. Brushed aside over hurdles on return from a break but much more like it when third at Down Royal 2 weeks ago, 5 lengths behind Dinoland.

Much improved for his current yard when landing handicap chases at Downpatrick (3m) and Tramore (2¾m) in May. Failed to complete the hat-trick switched to hurdling after a break but confirmed he's still in top form over the larger obstacles when second at Down Royal 2 weeks ago.

Successful over 25f at Cheltenham on New Year's Day before finding the spring festivals a shade too competitive. Runner-up in this race 12 months ago and leading amateur rider booked. Has to be of interest.

Quick off the mark for new yard when winning at Worcester and at Uttoxeter earlier this season. Kept busy since and got back on track after a couple of subdued efforts when placed the last twice, latterly over C&D 3 weeks ago fitted with a tongue tie for the first time.

Has taken well to chasing this season, winning 23f handicaps at Killarney in July and August before finding another jolt of improvement for latest success at Roscommon. Shaped as though still in form when fourth at Down Royal 2 weeks ago, though was behind 2 re-opposing rivals.

Has quickly made up into a better chaser than hurdler, winning a pair of Worcester handicaps in August/September. Lost his unbeaten record but shaped well when third over C&D under this rider 3 weeks ago and in a change of headgear, he remains of interest.

Won 3m handicap hurdles at Wexford and Bellewstown in 2025. Has made a promising start over fences for Denis Hogan, not always fluent but still finished runner-up in the Cork National (3½m) 2 weeks ago, Unexposed as a stayer.

Lightly raced for his age and enhanced good strike rate over fences in 7-runner handicap chase at Carlisle (25f) in February, staying on well. Could manage only fifth at Sandown a month later and mark looks about right (sixth in last year's renewal).

Back to form with a bang during the spring, winning Edinburgh National and solid efforts in Sussex National/Bet365 Gold Cup. Always on the back foot following an early mistake returned to chasing at Ascot 2 weeks ago and better expected in a change of headgear. Won this from 2 lb lower in 2024.

Has never stood much racing but having left Olly Murphy for £16,000 in May, he showed much more than previous 2 attempts over fences when second of 7 at Ffos Las a month ago (3½m). This is a deeper race, though.

Irish point winner who scored twice in staying handicap hurdles last season and was going the right way in the spring. Should make his mark over fences at some point but both starts last month fairly low key. Could hardly be in better hands though as he goes back up in distance.

label: 13:10 Cheltenham
race: JCB Triumph Trial Juvenile Hurdle (Registered As the Prestbury Juvenile Hurdle) (Grade 2) (Gbb Race) (Class 1) (Turf) 3YO only 2m 87y Winner: £47,552 (9 runners)
note: James Owen has won 2 of the last 3 renewals and has a good chance of adding to that tally with CHARLES DARNAY, who looks another very useful juvenile for connections after his listed win at Wetherby. Irish challengers Atomic City and Admiral Will Brown were both impressive when making winning debuts in this sphere so rate as serious threats.

runners.tf_comment: Flat winner for this yard and made a winning start over hurdles in good style fitted with a tongue strap at Down Royal (a race won by subsequent Grade 1 winners Wodhooh and Mange Tout in recent years) 2 weeks ago, leading on bridle between 3 and 2 out. Needs considering.
Flat maiden winner on heavy ground in the spring and looked potentially useful when making a successful hurdling debut with a fair amount in hand in Cork maiden 5 weeks ago. On the shortlist.

Progressive winner on the Flat and overcame inexperience (took time to warm to his task) to make a successful start in this sphere in listed event at Wetherby 2 weeks ago. That is just about the best form on offer and he rates an exciting prospect.

Maiden winner on the Flat in Ireland for Jessica Harrington. Progressed as expected from his gentle introduction to hurdling when 5¾ lengths fourth to Charles Darnay in listed event at Wetherby but has work to do to turn around the form with that one. Headgear on (well held when tried on Flat).

Progressive form in the spring for Mme M. Pineda, winning at Compiegne on third start. Changed hands for €150,000 after and only just failed to make a winning start for this yard at Market Rasen 3 weeks ago, an error 2 out and his awkwardness under pressure costing him. Headgear now applied.
Flat winner who's out of a half-sister to very smart hurdler/smart chase winner (2m-19f winner) Grey Shot, but this looks a very tall order on hurdles bow.

Useful stayer on the Flat but will need to jump with a lot more confidence in order to reach similar heights over hurdles given the manner of his hurdles debut win at Wetherby last month, rallying to lead close home after some iffy jumps. Yard also saddles Charles Darnay.

Magic Dream gelding. Dam, winner on Flat in Norway, half-sister to smart hurdler/useful chaser Colonel Mustard. Showed ability sole run on Flat before winning newcomer hurdle event at Clairefontaine in June, staying on well to lead late on. Sold from Mathieu Pitart for €155,000 soon after.

Modest form on the Flat before making a winning hurdling debut at Hexham in June. Hasn't progressed since, though, and looks out of his depth starting out for a new yard (sold from Dan Skelton for £5,500).

label: 13:45 Cheltenham
race: Paddy Power Arkle Challenge Trophy Trial Novices' Chase (Grade 2) (Gbb Race) (Class 1) (Turf) 4YO+ 1m 7f 199y Winner: £47,552 (6 runners)
note: An exciting early-season clash. The mightily impressive OLD PARK STAR looks the one to beat if reproducing the pick of his hurdling form, with the potential for even better to come over fences. Kabral Du Mathan's only defeat since joining Dan Skelton came when a blatant non-stayer in the Stayers' Hurdle. He's a most worthy adversary with last month's impressive chasing debut success under his belt.

runners.tf_comment: Fairly useful filly. Steadily improved over fences in France. Created a positive impression when decisively winning a 3-runner event on stable debut/return, the runner-up franking the form earlier this week. Stiff task against Kabral Du Mathan/Old Park Star, even in receipt of 15 lb.

Enthusiastic front runner. Highly progressive when landing a chase hat-trick at Uttoxeter (2m) in June. Forgivable effort in the Summer Hurdle prior to capitalising on a soft lead in a 4-runner event at Kelso last time. Tall order to extend his winning sequence over fences in this company.

Highly impressive over hurdles last season. Touch of Altior about the performance when making it 4-4 in the Supreme Novice, leaving the impression we've yet to see the best of him. Most exciting chasing prospect, for all his yard has a comparatively poor record in this race (2 wins in 48 years).

Progressive front runner. Jumped impeccably when completing a hat-trick in another small field at Hexham last month. Progressed again when losing his unbeaten chase record to a once-smart hurdler over C&D latest. Tough ask up in class, especially with competition for the lead this time.

Useful sort. Strong-travelling display when completing a double in Galway Hurdle this summer. Off the mark over fences at second time of asking in workmanlike style at Sligo in September (had a spin of Flat since). Stronger pace should suit here, though has plenty to find on bare form.

Flying too high in the Champion Hurdle last season. Supported the notion he'll be better over fences when scoring easily on chasing debut. Jumping again looked an asset when turned over at Roscommon (soft) in June. Back on more suitable ground and likely best of the rest behind the market leaders.

Smart 6-y-o who looked right at home at the top level before his stamina gave way in the Stayers Hurdle in March. Jumped impeccably when easily making a winning start over fences at Perth on return. More success to come this season and could well make this a stern opening test for Old Park Star.

label: 14:20 Cheltenham
race: Paddy Power Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (Gbb Race) (Class 1) (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 4f 44y Winner: £91,120 (13 runners)
note: A typically competitive renewal of the Paddy Power with preference going to BLUEKING D'OROUX, who improved since being fitted with headgear for Paul Nicholls and makes his debut for Dan Skelton over a track and trip that should suit his prominent-racing style. Madara was a revelation when winning the Plate at the Festival and has to be respected after a spin over hurdles, whilst fellow Festival winner Meetmebythesea remains unexposed and can continue to improve in his second season over fences.

runners.tf_comment: Smart hurdler who took a step forward over fences when just denied in handicap at Kempton in March and signed off last season with a good second in the Manifesto Novices' Chase at Aintree (2½m). Run style should suit this test and he holds strong claims on first start for Dan Skelton.

Has thrived over fences this summer, scoring 4 times in small-field contests at up to 23f. Last 2 defeats shouldn't necessarily be taken to suggest that the handicapper has caught up with him, things not panning out ideally at Warwick last time, but this would require a clear career best.

Enhanced his excellent record fresh when winning at Warwick (2½m, soft) in February. Brought down early at the Cheltenham Festival next time before respectable fourth of 17 in the Veterans' Final at Haydock, though proved disappointing on this season's comeback run at Ffos Las last month.

Several good efforts in top handicap chases, returning from a breathing operation to land the Ultima at the Festival (25f, good to soft) in March. Emerged with credit when fourth in the Grand National last time but returns from a 7-month break over a trip short of his optimum.

Made a winning chase bow at Limerick before producing a smart effort to follow up in 2m Grade 2 at this meeting 12 months ago. Shaped quite well until her stamina gave way when fourth of 9 in Champion Novices' Chase at Punchestown (25f) in April and her opening looks workable with O'Keeffe aboard.

Bounced back to best under a more patient ride when winning a premier handicap over C&D on New Year's Day. Has failed by a long way to back that up in 4 subsequent starts, tailed off when falling 3 out at Ayr (2m, heavy) back in April. Solid record fresh and handicapper given him a squeak, however.

Continued his improvement switched to fences when scoring at Wetherby and Ayr either side of last Christmas before taking his record in this sphere to 3-4 when powering clear to win the 18-runner Golden Miller (21f) at the Festival. That form worked out well and type to progress further this season.

Posted plenty of solid efforts for Willie Mullins last season, including when sixth in the Plate over C&D in March. Finally shed his maiden tag over fences second time out for this yard when winning a 9-runner handicap chase over C&D (good) 3 weeks ago but more needed to take this after 4 lb rise.

Took well to chasing last year despite failing to get his head in front, finishing a very good third of 22 in the Ultima at Cheltenham (25f, good to soft). Failed to capitalise on what looked a good opportunity at Newton Abbot 4 weeks ago (hit 1.03 in running) but yard has fine record in this race.

Hard to knock his form in handicaps last season, finishing fourth in the Grand Annual at the Festival. Rare jumping lapse saw him unseat early at Punchestown last time but others look better treated after 6 months off.
Smart handicap chaser who rather picked up the pieces when staying on into third in the Charlie Hall Chase at Wetherby (3m, good) 14 days ago. Work to be done from this mark, though.

Held his form well last season and gained reward when winning 3-runner event at Chepstow on final start, albeit in a race that fell apart in front of him. Proved he's still on the up when winning 8-runner handicap chase at Ffos Las (19f, soft) 31 days ago but this is tougher again after 5 lb rise.

Bagged a pair of handicap chases at Killarney and over C&D last October. Turned in some good efforts in defeat after, including fifth of 23 in the Plate at the Festival and he should be sharper for his recent comeback run at Limerick, though mark looks about right and O'Keeffe prefers July Flower.

Smart chaser who won the Plate over C&D at the Festival prior to a typically strong-travelling display when third in the Topham in April. Shaped with plenty of encouragement on his recent comeback outing over hurdles at Carlisle and he makes plenty of appeal with cheekpieces back on.

Progressive chaser who won a pair of small-field Sandown handicaps (soft) last season. Only denied a hat-trick by a smart one in a big-field listed handicap at the Punchestown Festival and he can continue on his upward curve returning from a 6-month break.

label: 14:55 Cheltenham
race: From the Horses Mouth Podcast Handicap Hurdle (Gbb Race) (Class 2) (Turf) 4YO+ 2m 7f 208y Winner: £19,061 (16 runners)
note: Preference is for IFIWEREARICHMAN, who has looked in good form over hurdles this season without being seen to best effect. He could be ready to open his account for the campaign racing from 8 lb below his mark over fences, though Ace of Spades isn't taken lightly for the Skeltons with his reappearance run behind him. Rambo T could also be in the mix.

runners.tf_comment: Showed improved form last season, winning twice including a Pertemps qualifier at Huntingdon (25f) in January. Found things tougher at the Festival and at Aintree, but shaped as if he would step forward from the run when mid-field over this C&D 3 weeks ago. Respected.

Smart at best on the Flat (stays 1¾m) and has been getting the hang of things over hurdles, making it back-to-back handicap wins at Sedgefield when getting the better of William Yeats over 21f last month. Up in grade but could still have more to offer given his ability on the level.

Losing run is mounting up but in first-time blinkers he ran better than for a while when second of 14 in handicap at Cork (2½m) 13 days ago, though was held when left second at the last. Task is now to build on his latest run back up in trip.

Landed a listed chase for Willie Mullins last season before losing his way over fences. Got back on track reverted to hurdles when winning minor event at Thurles in March, but ran poorly the next twice and well held in a pair of handicaps for this yard, the latest over C&D 3 weeks ago.

Gained a first handicap success over hurdles when scoring comfortably at Wincanton (21f) in April. Again travelled well when following up at Uttoxeter (23f), so task is now to pick up where he left off after 6-month break in this tougher race.

Ready winner at Hereford (3¼m) in April and has returned to form the last twice, taking second close home in 19-runner contest over this C&D 3 weeks ago. Has now placed on both visits to this track and he can give another good account.

Began the year in fine form for Gavin Gromwell, runner-up on first 2 outings (over fences on the second occasion). However, has struggled for form over both hurdles/fences for present stable, pulled up in the Irish Grand National when last seen 7 months ago.

Won his first 5 starts (3 bumpers, 2 hurdles) and bounced back from a below-par run in Grade 1 novice at Aintree in spring 2025 when third in listed event at Perth. Gave his running after 7 months off when fifth of 17 on handicap debut at Haydock, but has been absent almost a year since.

Useful winner over fences and has been shaping well from his lower mark over hurdles this season, meeting trouble in running when sixth of 14 in handicap at Listowel (2½m) 7 weeks ago. Yard has been going well and he makes plenty of appeal up in trip.

Useful hurdler who didn't quite match that level over fences last season, though did win a Down Royal handicap in January. Mixed form in 3 subsequent outings, pulled up at Ballinrobe when last seen in May. Reverts to hurdles and switches to a visor on first run since leaving Gordon Elliott.

Won handicap chases at around 2½m on first 2 starts for current yard in 2024/25. However, his form went the wrong way last season and fared no better back over hurdles when mid-field in handicap at Punchestown (23f) in April. Hood reapplied after 6 months off.

Opened his account in novice at Cork (17f) in May but hasn't managed to reproduce that form since, beaten 16¼ lengths when fourth of 13 in handicap at Punchestown (2½m) last month. Engaged 1.10 at this course on Friday.

Winner of the Silver Trophy at Chepstow (19f) last year but didn't kick on from that effort the remainder of the campaign. After 5 months off, ran well when fifth of 17 in a stronger renewal of the Chepstow race in October and he's now 4 lb below his last winning mark. Merits consideration.

Recorded a 4-timer in first half of 2025 and added to his tally at Uttoxeter (2½m) in May, though was seen to good effect in a soundly-run race. Failed to repeat that effort in listed handicap (2¾m) at the Galway festival and has stamina to prove upped further in trip.

After 5 months off, made second start for this trainer a winning one in handicap at Sedgefield (2½m) in August. Progressed again when runner-up to Aimeric at the same course next 2 starts, before overcoming the run of the race when scoring at Newcastle (3m) 9 days ago.

Fairly useful stayer on the Flat who made it 4 wins from 9 starts over hurdles when scoring in handicap at Newbury in February last year. Also made the frame at this venue on 3 occasions and yard has won this race twice in the last 5 years, though has 20-month absence to overcome.

label: 15:30 Cheltenham
race: Paddy Power Intermediate Handicap Hurdle (Class 3) (Turf) 3YO+ 2m 5f Winner: £14,976 (10 runners)
note: MONEYGARROW hardly damaged his stock when eighth in the Albert Bartlett here in March and looks very interesting tackling handicap company for the first time. He gets the nod over Daylatedollarshort, whose Silver Trophy form is proving strong, with Sunny South West, Hillberry Hill and A King Of Magic all lurking on potentially handy marks.

runners.tf_comment: Most progressive as a 4-y-o last season, only denied a hat-trick by a useful improver at Punchestown in April. Picked up where he left off when winning a strong renewal of the Silver Trophy at Chepstow (19f) on return. Further progress to come back up in trip and no surprise to see him follow up.

Lightly-raced 6-y-o. Settled better/looked more the finished article when opening his account in style in Market Rasen maiden (21f) in April, the runner-up since franking the form. Needs more again up in class on handicap bow/return, though is still unexposed at the trip.

Runner-up in last year's renewal of this race. Progressed again to notch a third handicap hurdle success at Naas (2m, heavy) in February. Encouraging comeback when 3½ lengths behind new stablemate Luck Between Us latest. Respected off higher British mark with talented 5-lb claimer taking over.

Won back-to-back small-field events last December. Strong form when placing on third straight handicap start at Fakenham in May. Back on the up to some tune when easily winning on return at Fontwell (19f). Type who'll go on improving for a good yard, however, this demands a fair bit more.

Saw off Grand Conqueror before progressing again to land a double in smooth style at Newbury in February. Better than he showed on both subsequent starts, latterly on comeback at Chepstow. Usual promising claimer on and entitled to be closer to form in a stronger handicap than previously contested.

Chasing type who won a maiden at the second attempt for Ms Margaret Mullins last winter. Changed hands for £70,000 prior to easily defying a penalty in a weak Southwell novice (2½m) on stable debut in March. Likely to progress further and opening mark potentially lenient as he bids for a hat-trick.

Developed into a fairly useful hurdler since returning to handicaps. Smoothly made it 3 wins from his last 4 starts at Listowel (2½m) on final start for Donncha Duggan in September. Eye-catching jockey booking on stable debut, but an 8 lb rise probably prevents a hat-trick. Engaged 3.30 here Friday.

Fairly useful type. Backed up his breakthrough hurdle success at Naas with creditable efforts in graded company last season. Well held in the Martin Pipe at the Festival subsequently. Likely to again find his British mark beyond him, even with a recent pipe-opener under his belt.

Well-related sort who chased home Ballyfad (now very useful) in a point. Decisively off the mark with sound-jumping display at Hereford in March. Progressed again to follow up (2-2 under this claimer) on return/handicap bow at Uttoxeter (2½m). Hat-trick may prove beyond him in a deeper event.

Useful bumper scorer. Off the mark on the Flat prior to shaping second best (took time to warm to task) when 4¼ lengths fourth of 11 at this course (2½m) latest. Could be better to come on just his third handicap start, with top Irish claimer again taking the ride.

Low-mileage 5-y-o. Very much on the up at the close of last season. Relished the step up to 2½m (travelled with much more purpose) when comprehensively beating a couple of last-time-out winners at Perth in April. Open to further improvement for top yard, for all this is a step up in class.

Cracksman gelding. Half-brother to smart hurdler Luccia. Aided by the favourite failing to keep straight when narrowly defying a penalty at Kempton (2m) on third and final start for Nicky Henderson. Likely needs a chunk of improvement to complete a hat-trick on handicap/stable debut.

Well-related point/bumper winner. Progressed to win back-to-back races (solid form) at Warwick/Windsor last winter. Promised even better for a long way when 16½ lengths eighth of 22 in Grade 1 Albert Bartlett here (3m) in March. Drop back in trip no issue and looks very interesting on handicap bow.

label: 16:00 Cheltenham
race: Karndean Designflooring Mares' Open Nh Flat Race (Listed) (Gbb Race) (Class 1) (Turf) 4YO to 5YO 2m 87y Winner: £11,888 (13 runners)
note: An excellent renewal of this listed bumper. ELEGANTEMENTE created a fine impression when forging 6 lengths clear of the reopposing She Was The One on her debut at Ballinrobe in August and, with much better to come, is taken to maintain her unbeaten record up in grade. Soleretta must be held in some regard by her yard for Harry Skelton to side with her over Northern Singer, who landed a recent Chepstow bumper in good style. Miss Master and impressive Stratford winner Gypsy Sky are also feared.

runners.tf_comment: Built on a promising start at Sligo when awarded similar race there in July (second past the post but subsequently promoted having suffered interference). Backed up that form when third under a penalty at Down Royal but may find this test too sharp.

Sea The Stars mare who made a successful debut in 14-runner bumper (5/2) at Punchestown (2m, good to soft) on NH debut 32 days ago, suited by emphasis on speed. More on her plate tackling better company but still warrants respect with conditions likely to suit once again.

No Risk At All filly who looked a useful prospect when winning 11-runner bumper at Ballinrobe (2m) on debut in August, by 6 lengths from She Was The One, forging clear. Looks sure to go on to better things and is the form pick.

Well-bred Jack Hobbs filly who overcame inexperience and the run of the race to make a winning debut in quite taking fashion in 8-runner bumper at Stratford (2m) last month. That form has since been franked by the placed horses and she seems sure to progress.

Jet Away filly who won sole start in point bumpers and offered something to work on switched to Rules when 9½ lengths second of 14 in bumper at Aintree in May. Subsequently sold out of Myles Osborne's yard for £45,000 but needs a big step forward in this grade.
Mastercraftsman filly from a smart Flat family and well worth a look in the betting for a yard which has done well with its runners in Britain over the years. Wears tongue strap.

£48,000 4-y-o, Masterstroke filly. Dam (b84), ran once in bumper, half-sister to high-class hurdler/smart chaser (stayed 3m) Dedigout. Won sole outing in points by 4 lengths from reopposing She Was The One, so warrants respect on Rules debut having joined promising yard.

Passing Glance mare who dead-heated for first sole outing in point bumpers but was outpaced from the home turn in a steadily-run bumper at Newton Abbot on recent Rules debut. Looks one for longer trips later on.

Order of St George filly who was bought for €80,000 after finishing runner-up on sole outing in Irish points in March. That form has already been franked by the winner, so shouldn't be completely overlooked.

Pether's Moon filly. Dam unraced half-sister to French hurdlers/chasers (15f-2¾m winner) Saint Goustan Blue and (17f-19f winner) Viola St Goustan. Yard's newcomers warrant respect, but this is a tough starting point all the same.

£22,000 3-y-o, Order of St George filly. Easy winner of sole start in Irish points and is a half-sister to bumper winner/useful hurdler My Sister Sarah, so shouldn't be overlooked, for all that this represents no easy assignment on her Rules debut.

Placed on second of 2 outings in points and improved to get off the mark at the third time of asking in bumpers when making all in 14-runner event at Listowel (2m) in late-September. Well worth her place in this better company.

£145,000 Maxios filly. Dam sister to fairly useful hurdler Gold In The Rivers and half-sister to useful hurdler/chase winner Wait For Me. Sure to have won when fell last only start in Irish points in March and it could be significant Harry Skelton has elected to ride her instead of Northern Singer.

£54,000 purchase after running out easy winner of her second Irish point in April and, fitted with a hood, showed plenty of speed when following up in 8-runner bumper at Chepstow last month. Rates a useful prospect, but Harry Skelton does desert her for Soleretta.

Walk In The Park mare. Half-sister to useful hurdler/chaser Queens Gamble, stays 2½m, and bumper winner Brosna Queen. Produced a promising first effort when 12¼ lengths third of 12 to a smart sort at Fairyhouse on sole outing for Mrs Lorna Fowler in April. Open to improvement for new yard.

label: 12:07 Uttoxeter
race: Quinnbet Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Class 5) (Turf) 3YO+ 2m 3f 207y Winner: £3,697 (8 runners)
note: SPARTAN TIMES returns from a short break with his yard continuing in excellent order and given there's still scope from his current mark based on his Flat form, he could be the answer. Lunar Orbit and French recruit Zeus Forlonge head the opposition.

runners.tf_comment: Scored twice at up to 2½m over hurdles last summer. Back to form when second over hurdles at Worcester (23f) in August but looks one with problems suddenly judged on next 3 efforts.

Ground-versatile sort who won 4 times around 2½m last season. Hard to derive much promise from his first 3 outings this autumn but eased a further 2 lb and much more like it when second of 8 at Worcester 3 weeks ago. Cheekpieces back on.

Fairly useful on the Flat. Justified support to land a Market Rasen juvenile in December. Runner-up twice for Dan Skelton, latterly when displaying improved form against a thriving rival at Hereford 3 weeks ago. Has to command respect but he can pull hard so no easy ride for a conditional.

Successful between the flags and handicap debut fourth of 15 at Newcastle in February was a step in the right direction. Fitted with a tongue tie when third over 23f at Bangor in March, seeing it out well. Off since and yard yet to fully fire this season.
Progressive form in a trio of maiden hurdles in Ireland for Edward F. Power this summer. Moved yards ahead of this handicap debut but mark demands that he continues to improve.

Shrugged off any element of rustiness with a battling display when making a winning handicap debut here in May (2m). Runner-up twice on the level since and possible excuse for both efforts in this sphere, reportedly finishing lame in September. Given a break and yard in form.

Low-mileage 6-y-o who produced an improved effort in first-time cheekpieces when runner-up at Hereford (2m) in May. Easy to back when failing to reproduce that form at Stratford but returned from 5 months off minus cheekpieces with a sound effort at that venue. Headgear back on.
Half-brother to 7 winners and claimed on the back of an improved showing when runner-up at Auteuil in May. Upped slightly in trip and has to command serious respect given the yard he's joined.

label: 12:42 Uttoxeter
race: Somersby Novices' Hurdle (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO+ 1m 7f 168y Winner: £5,446 (9 runners)
note: Bumper/hurdles winner SPANISH DARLING didn't look out of place when fourth pitched into a Grade 2 on just his second hurdles start at Cheltenham 3 weeks ago, within a length of the lead prior to fluffing his lines at the last. Firmly remaining with his best days ahead of him, he's impossible to oppose returned to much calmer waters. Bumper winner Port Isaac and newcomers Made For Mary and Montevallo may emerge next best.

runners.tf_comment: Fair winner up to 1m on all-weather this year but ended the season on a low-key note and at long odds, he went with no promise when pulled up in a C&D novice on hurdles debut 7 days ago.

Maiden pointer who exceeded expectations on Rules debut when fourth of 12 in maiden chase at Kilbeggan (2½m) in June. However, couldn't replicate that when well held over hurdles at Roscommon on final start for Donncha Duggan in August. Made an interesting yard switch but possibly one for later on.

Fair form when winning first of 2 starts in bumpers initially this season. Related to several hurdle winners but fitted with a hood, she was given a considerate introduction when fourth in a mares maiden (17f) at Newton Abbot in July. This promises to reveal more now debuting for new yard.

€24,000 3-y-o, Blue Bresil filly. Dam (b89), point/bumper winner, half-sister to winning hurdler/top-class chaser (stays 3¼m) Conflated. Pedigree offers hope debuting for stable who continue amongst the winners and support behind her would look interesting.

€52,000 3-y-o, Maxios gelding. Dam (c124/h112) 2½m/21f hurdle/chase winner (stayed 23f). Made frame both starts in Irish points, runner-up last time (Feb 2026) and worth noting if supported in the betting ahead of Rules/hurdles debut.

Linda's Lad gelding who got off the mark in points at second attempt in May but went off a big price and showed nothing on hurdles debut at Southwell 12 days ago, losing touch back straight. Can only be watched.

Knew what was required when making a winning debut in tidy fashion in 6-runner event at Doncaster in March. Had something to find up in class but ran no sort of race even so following 8 months off at Cheltenham 3 weeks ago. Not one to write off now hurdling and another best guided by the betting.

Modest maiden on Flat. Big prices and little to shout about on first 2 hurdle runs but not seen to best effect (also caught eye of stewards) when fourth on qualifying run in a C&D maiden 6 weeks ago. Remains capable of better, not least in handicaps.

Built on debut promise when landing Worcester bumper (2m) in September and even better when following up in maiden hurdle over same C&D a month later. Didn't look at all out of place when fourth pitched into Grade 2 at Cheltenham since, fluffing his lines last. Hard to beat back in calmer waters.

label: 13:15 Uttoxeter
race: Carlsberg EBF Mares' 'National Hunt' Maiden Hurdle (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO to 6YO 2m 3f 207y Winner: £5,809 (7 runners)
note: MALINA ROAD laid down solid foundations in a trio of bumper starts last winter, including success at listed level and with this increase in trip promising to suit now hurdling, she shades preference over Boombox who went agonisingly close to making a successful stable/hurdling debut at Worcester recently. Bumper scorer Kentford Legacy hails from a yard in form and also commands a second look, as does Port And Brandy.

runners.tf_comment: Placed on 3 completed starts in points and finished second only start in bumpers for S. Curling at Killarney in May. Changed hands for £110,000 thereafter and went agonisingly close to making a winning yard/hurdles debut at Worcester (2m) in October. Expected to build on that and one to consider.

£120,000 purchase after winning sole start in Irish points. Steady progress in 3 bumper starts, third at Ludlow (2m) in April but looked one for later on/handicaps over hurdles when fifth of 7 in a C&D mares novice in May. Had breathing operation and looks best watched after 6 months off.

Stepped up a little on her debut form for Richard Bandey when second of 8 in bumper at Catterick (2m, good) in March. Similar form when fourth of 7 in a bumper at this course on return in October and likely more will be needed if she's to feature now hurdling.

Scorpion mare from a good jumping family who overcame inexperience to make a winning debut in a Fontwell bumper (2¼m, good, 22/1) in May, going in snatches but ultimately well on top at finish. Very much the type to make her mark over hurdles with her stable amongst the winners.

Won completed start in Irish points and successful on 2 of her 3 starts in bumpers last winter, latterly a listed event at Market Rasen (17f) in January. Lost her unbeaten record conceding weight all round when third at Newbury in February but she's a bright prospect now hurdling over a longer trip.

Little impact in a pair of bumpers but she built on her hurdles debut fifth when third in mares maiden over this trip at Hereford in March. Faced a stiff task when fifth in listed company next time and whilst this less demanding, others still appeal much more.

Made the frame both starts in bumpers and upped in trip for her hurdles bow, she posted a fair effort when second of 7 in a C&D mares novice back in May. That form may not be as good as first impressions would imply but a repeat gives her sound claims of being in the mix again.

label: 13:50 Uttoxeter
race: Karina's 60th Birthday Celebration Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle (Class 5) (Turf) 3YO+ 1m 7f 168y Winner: £3,697 (12 runners)
note: CHAMBERS is well treated on his Flat form and having won his latest start in that sphere, he's fancied to make a successful handicap hurdle debut. Arcon didn't immediately improve on his handicap bow but looks capable of making an impact in this sort of company, whilst Prince Phil can improve handicapping.

runners.tf_comment: Fairly useful stayer on Flat (stays 2m). Caught the eye of the stewards at Uttoxeter in July before not really taking to brush hurdles at Worcester on qualifying run later that month. Didn't immediately improve making handicap debut at this C&D (good) 41 days ago but likely still capable of more.
Placed on completed start in points but no solid form under Rules.

Fair winner on Flat (up to 2m) in 2025 for George Boughey. Still looked a bit rough around the edges when fourth on handicap debut at Worcester in June but was below that level there the following month. Others preferred back from a break.

No impact in starts over hurdles in May/June but he's a fair sort on the Flat and has won twice on the level since last seen over obstacles, including at Southwell late last month. Clearly has a workable opening mark on that form now back over hurdles.

Signs of ability on the Flat for Karl Burke but there have been very few positives to take from his efforts in this sphere so far, jumping awkwardly prior to pulling up on last month's handicap debut at Worcester.
Minor promise in bumpers last season but showed little in 3 starts over hurdles subsequently for Sarah-Jayne Davies. Worth betting check making handicap debut for new yard after 7 months off.
Runner-up both starts in Irish points but nothing to shout about over hurdles so far, pulled up after racing freely on last month's handicap debut.

Fair form when runner-up twice from 3 starts in French bumpers. Well below that level in a couple of starts over hurdles, for all he shaped a bit better than the bare result when sixth of 7 in novice hurdle (66/1) at Fontwell (19f, good to soft) 30 days ago. Makes handicap hurdle debut.

Shaped as if better for the run but still surpassed the form of a couple of low-key efforts in Plumpton handicaps when fourth of 9 in novice hurdle at Cartmel (17f, good) in August. Seemed to back that form up when fifth in a Sedgefield maiden last month but might need more back in a handicap.
Showed a bit on bumper debut and though he failed to make an impact in 3 quick qualifying runs in the spring, he appeals as one who should do better now handicapping after a 6-month break.

Showed a bit when hitting the frame in a Newton Abbot bumper in July. Looks to be being brought along with handicaps in mind over hurdles, not unduly punished when fourth of 6 in novice hurdle (50/1) at that same course (17f, good) 47 days ago. Makes handicap bow having since left David Pipe.

Showed a fair level of ability in 2 Irish bumpers for Stuart Crawford but has yet to better modest form over hurdles, finishing only eighth on March's 2m Warwick handicap debut with a tongue tie added (retained). Returns from 8 months off here.

label: 14:25 Uttoxeter
race: Eaton Hall Shooting Ground Mares' Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO+ 1m 7f 214y Winner: £5,281 (4 runners)
note: A trappy mares handicap which can go the way of the experienced IRISH CHORUS, who did well in this sphere last season and was unable to recover from a late blunder on her recent comeback. Lau And Shaz had a positive time of things over hurdles last campaign and should prove at least as good over fences, whilst Lady Tadita should also benefit from her initial experience chasing.

runners.tf_comment: Winless over hurdles but different story over fences, winning 3 handicaps around 2m last season. Another good effort when second at Warwick in May. Pitching for a place when making a serious error 3 out on return at Huntingdon earlier this month, and she makes appeal back against her own sex.

Debut bumper winner and looked an even better prospect when winning her first 2 starts over hurdles last season, before a good second in listed mares novice at Taunton in December. However, was tailed off at Huntingdon in February and looked in need of the experience on her recent C&D chase debut.

Back to her best when making a successful stable debut in Wincanton novice on Boxing Day. Led until crumpling on landing 4 out at Windsor prior to resuming winning ways at Hereford. Anchored by a double penalty at Taunton in April but she appeals as one who should make a chaser this season.

Scored over hurdles at Hexham in October and largely in good form subsequently, signing off for the campaign when a good second of 15 in 21f handicap at Newbury in March. Made the frame in a point and she's not without hope sent chasing after having a breathing operation during the summer.

label: 15:00 Uttoxeter
race: Hobgoblin Handicap Chase (Gbb Race) (Class 4) (Turf) 4YO+ 3m 10y Winner: £5,281 (8 runners)
note: ORDEROFTHEDAY ought to relish this step back up in trip, and he's taken to make it 2 wins from 3 starts over fences. Kahavari will be suited by speed-favouring conditions and just edges Kalhandrion for next best.

runners.tf_comment: Had been knocking on the door prior to coming out on top in sprint finish in a 4-runner chase at Sandown (2½m) in April. Probably needed his reappearance at Wetherby last time. Back up in trip and entitled to do better in race that could develop into a relative test of speed.

Half-brother to Valadom (useful chaser for connections). Impressed when making all to double his tally at Exeter (3m, heavy) before running better than the beaten distance might suggest final start last season. Goes well fresh, though relatively untested under these conditions over fences.

Winning pointer/hurdler. Found plenty to make a successful chasing debut here (2½m) in May. Entitled to come on for last month's comeback at Perth (beaten 17 lengths). Sets the standard on the pick of his form and remains capable of better stepping back up in trip.

Successful sole outing in points. Well-backed second on debut at Chepstow in April. More professional than on return when runner-up in first-time visor here (2½m) latest. Opening mark demands more, but he looks the type who could improve for the step back up in trip/quick switch to fences.

Third sole start in Irish points. Clearly hasn't been easy to train since making an impressive winning start over hurdles in March 2024. Returns 23 months on from a modest chasing debut and is probably the stable second string.

Won sole start in bumpers. Progressed into a fairly useful stayer when completing a handicap hurdle double at Doncaster in December. Underlined that consistency isn't his strong suit with 2 subsequent runs last season. Claims on pick of his form, for all others look more obvious chasing types.

Flat-bred 5-y-o with a good course record. Went close to snapping a 2-year losing run over hurdles here (23f) in September. Race fitness on his side when only beaten by a stronger stayer in big-field handicap at Chepstow (3m) since. Makes belated chasing debut and others perhaps have more scope.

From a good jumping family. Picked up for £42,000 after placing in a couple of points. Fairly useful winner on handicap hurdle bow at Uttoxeter (2½m, heavy) penultimate start last season. Stable has had several ready to roll in recent weeks, and he looks first string on jockey bookings.

label: 15:35 Uttoxeter
race: 1664 Biere Open Nh Flat Race (Gbb Race) (Class 5) (Turf) 4YO to 5YO 1m 7f 168y Winner: £2,451 (12 runners)
note: JIMMY GATZ is well worth another chance to build on his strong debut form having probably found testing conditions against him at Ffos Las when last seen (Flat bred). Bateleur went down fighting on his Rules debut at Sedgefield last month and his excellent attitude is sure to stand him in good stead again, while the selection's stablemate, Hannah's Kitchen, is the pick of the newcomers before market clues.

runners.tf_comment: €30,000 3-y-o, £6,000 5-y-o, Feel Like Dancing gelding. Half-brother to fair hurdler Kells Priory, stays 25f. Wears tongue strap for Rules debut and makes little appeal based on his pointing exploits.

€3,000 3-y-o, Tirwanako gelding. Successful on his only start in point bumpers and, having attracted support, produced a promising first effort under Rules when second at Sedgefield last month, going down fighting. Likely to be on the premises again with his attitude sure to stand him in good stead.

€68,000 3-y-o, Poet's Word gelding. Half-brother to fairly useful hurdler/useful chaser Classic Maestro. Dam unraced half-sister to 19f bumper winner/fairly useful hurdle winner up to 23f Present In Court. Wears tongue strap for debut and the market should offer up some clues.
Masterstroke gelding. Dam unraced half-sister to fairly useful hurdler/useful chaser (stayed 3¼m) Merry King. Bred more for stamina than speed and stable has an ordinary strike rate in bumpers.
€55,000 3-y-o, Blue Bresil gelding. Dam unraced sister to multiple bumper winner/useful hurdler (2m winner) The Model Kingdom. Highly respected on debut for excellent yard.

Son of The Grey Gatsby who shaped encouragingly when fourth of 7 in a warm Carlisle bumper (17f) on his debut in February. Not in the same form at Ffos Las but was probably unsuited by testing conditions and well worth another chance back from 8 months off.

Well backed and knew her job when making a winning debut in 9-runner bumper at Bangor (17f, good) in April, seeing off a pair with experience in a close finish. More needed now taking on the boys under a penalty, though.

Shaped well in coming from the back to beat all bar one in a Hereford bumper on debut last November. Showed similar form when fifth in a warmer race at Kempton 3 months later and must enter calculations returning from another absence.

€80,000 No Risk At All gelding. Dam, ran once on Flat in France, half-sister to French chaser (stayed 2¾m) Quolibet. Runner-up sole start in Irish points (Apr 2026) and is another to consider on this switch to Rules.

Masked Marvel gelding. Dam, French hurdler/chaser (17f-21f winner), sister to French hurdler/chaser (17f-23f winner) Utopia Dream and fairly useful 3m hurdle winner Jakar du Moulin. Needs a market check for a yard which has its fair share of success in this sphere.
Heeraat gelding. Half-brother to 2 winners, including fair hurdler Gms Prince, stays 2¾m. Dam 9f-1½m winner. Yard knows this family well.

£30,000 4-y-o, Order of St George gelding. Half-brother to French 2¼m hurdle winner Lascaux. Dam, French hurdler (2¼m winner), half-sister to French hurdler/chaser (15f-19f winner) Laskaline. Runner-up sole start in Irish points (May 2026).
